service: Amazon Web Services Agent Registry is a managed catalog for publishing and discovering resources such as MCP servers, agents, and agent skills. Agent Registry Control is its control-plane API: use it to create and manage registries and the records they contain, configure discovery and authorization, govern record approval and curation workflows, and manage automatic detection of resources. Data-plane search and MCP invocation operations are provided by the companion Agent Registry API.

operations.AssociatePublisher: Associate a registry record with a publisher and assign the record a public identifier under the publisher's domain. The registry record must be APPROVED and the publisher must be ACTIVE. A registry record can have only one publisher association. The new association starts in PENDING_APPROVAL until a curator approves or rejects it. A ConflictException (HTTP 409) means the publisher is not ACTIVE yet, the registry record already has an association, or another registry record already holds the public identifier. To retry safely, repeat the request with the same clientToken; a retry returns the original association. If the publisher has reached its association quota, the request fails with ServiceQuotaExceededException (HTTP 402). Remove an unused association or request a quota increase.
operations.CreatePublisher: Create a publisher for a domain you control. The publisher starts in ACTION_REQUIRED, and the response includes a domainChallenge. To verify the domain, create a DNS TXT record with the challenge's recordName and recordValue. When the registry finds the record, the publisher becomes ACTIVE and you can associate registry records with it. Your account can have one publisher per domain. Creating a second publisher for the same domain fails with ConflictException unless the request repeats the original clientToken, which returns the existing publisher. The request also fails with ConflictException when another account has already verified the domain. If your account has reached its Publisher quota, the request fails with ServiceQuotaExceededException (HTTP 402). Delete an unused Publisher or request a quota increase.
operations.CreateRegistry: Creates a new registry, a catalog that organizes registry records and defines their discovery authorization and record approval behavior. Creation is asynchronous: the registry begins in the CREATING status and becomes usable once it reaches READY.
operations.CreateRegistryRecord: Creates a registry record within a registry. A registry record describes a discoverable resource, such as an MCP server, an agent, an agent skill, or a custom resource. For an agent skill, you can upload a skill package in artifact, or synchronize the skill from an Amazon S3 or GitHub source. Creation is asynchronous: the operation returns the record with the CREATING status while the registry processes it. If a GitHub user must first authorize access to the source, the operation returns the record with the CREATE_PENDING_AUTH status instead.
operations.DeletePublisher: Delete a publisher. A successful call returns an empty response. You can't delete a publisher that has registry record associations; disassociate every registry record from it first. The request fails with ConflictException while the publisher has associations or another delete is in progress. Association removals can take a few seconds to be reflected, so a delete that follows a disassociation can briefly fail with ConflictException; retry after a short wait. If the publisher ARN names your account and the publisher doesn't exist, the request fails with ResourceNotFoundException.
operations.DeleteRegistry: Deletes a registry. Deletion is asynchronous: the registry transitions to the DELETING status and is removed along with its registry records.
operations.DisassociatePublisher: Remove a registry record's publisher association and release its public identifier. A successful call returns an empty response. Disassociating a registry record that has no association succeeds. If another account created the association, the request fails with AccessDeniedException.
operations.GetPublisher: Get a publisher, including its verification status and the DNS challenge for its domain. If the publisher ARN names your account and the publisher doesn't exist, the request fails with ResourceNotFoundException.
operations.GetRegistry: Gets a registry by identifier (ARN or ID)
operations.GetRegistryRecord: Retrieves the details of a registry record. The response describes the record's latest revision, including a revision that isn't approved yet. For a skill record, the operation also returns the skill package in artifact and the source that the registry last synchronized the skill from in synchronizedSource.
operations.ListPublisherAssociations: List the registry record associations your account created. Pass publisherArn to list only the associations for that publisher; omit it to list associations across all publishers. Results are eventually consistent, so an association you just created or removed can take a few seconds to appear in or disappear from the list.
operations.ListPublishers: List the publishers your account owns, followed by the ACTIVE publishers shared with your account.
operations.ListRegistries: Lists the registries in the caller's account and Region, with optional filtering by status and discovery authorizer type
operations.ListRegistryRecords: Lists the registry records within a registry, with optional filtering by name, status, and record type
operations.ListTagsForResource: Lists the tags associated with the specified Amazon Web Services Agent Registry resource. Returns the current tag key-value pairs on the resource.
operations.SubmitRegistryRecordForApproval: Submits a DRAFT registry record for approval, moving it into the registry's approval workflow. Depending on the registry's approval configuration, the record is either auto-approved or set to PENDING_APPROVAL for a curator to approve or reject.
operations.TagResource: Adds or overwrites one or more tags for the specified Amazon Web Services Agent Registry resource. Tags are key-value pairs that you can use to categorize and manage Amazon Web Services resources. If a tag with the same key already exists on the resource, the service replaces its value with the value you specify.
operations.UntagResource: Removes one or more tags from the specified Amazon Web Services Agent Registry resource. The operation removes only the tags whose keys you supply; other tags on the resource remain unchanged.
operations.UpdatePublisherAssociationApprovalStatus: Record the curator's decision (APPROVED or REJECTED) on a registry record's publisher association. A successful call returns an empty response. Repeating the decision the association already holds changes nothing; the same approvalStatus with a different approvalStatusReason updates the reason. If the caller has no publisher association for the registry record, the request fails with AccessDeniedException. A ConflictException (HTTP 409) means the association is not in a state that accepts the decision (e.g. not PENDING_APPROVAL/APPROVED/REJECTED) or it changed while the request was being applied; read it again before deciding whether to resubmit.
operations.UpdateRegistry: Updates an existing registry. This operation uses PATCH semantics: specify only the fields you want to change, and omit the rest to leave them unchanged. Updates are applied asynchronously and the registry transitions to the UPDATING status while they are processed.
operations.UpdateRegistryRecord: Updates a registry record. The update is asynchronous: the operation returns the record with the UPDATING status while the registry processes it. If a GitHub user must first authorize access to the record's skill source, the operation returns the record with the UPDATE_PENDING_AUTH status instead. Fields that use update wrappers follow PATCH semantics: omit the field to leave it unchanged.
operations.UpdateRegistryRecordStatus: Updates the status of a registry record as part of the registry's curation workflow, for example to approve or reject a record that is pending approval, or to deprecate an approved record so that it is no longer discoverable
operations.ValidatePublisher: Restart domain verification for a publisher in FAILED or SUSPENDED. The publisher returns to ACTION_REQUIRED with a new domainChallenge, which the response includes. Update the DNS TXT record with the new recordValue; the previous value no longer verifies the domain. The request fails with ConflictException when the publisher is ACTIVE, verification is already in progress (ACTION_REQUIRED), or the publisher is being deleted.

BotCategory.base:
The category that describes a web bot's purpose. The categories follow AWS WAF Bot Control bot categories. Valid values:

  • advertising - Bots used for advertising, such as third-party ad services that access a website programmatically.

  • archiver - Bots that crawl the web and capture content to create archives.

  • content_fetcher - Bots that visit a website on behalf of a user to fetch content, such as RSS feeds, or to verify content.

  • email_client - Bots that check links in emails, such as those run by email providers to flag suspicious emails.

  • http_library - Requests generated by the HTTP libraries of programming languages, such as API clients.

  • link_checker - Bots that check for broken links.

  • miscellaneous - Bots that don't match another category.

  • monitoring - Bots that periodically access a website to monitor performance and uptime.

  • page_preview - Bots that generate page and link previews when content is shared on messaging, social media, or collaboration tools.

  • scraping_framework - Bots from web scraping frameworks that automate crawling and extracting website content.

  • search_engine - Bots that crawl websites to index content for search engine results.

  • security - Bots that scan web applications for vulnerabilities or perform security audits.

  • seo - Bots that crawl a website to help improve its search engine rankings.

  • social_media - Bots that social media platforms use to provide content summaries when users share content.

  • ai_training - AI bots that collect content to train AI models.

  • ai_search - AI bots that retrieve content to answer AI search queries.

  • ai_assistant - AI bots that access content on behalf of a user's AI assistant or agent.

  • ai_content_optimization - AI bots that analyze content to optimize it for AI-generated results.

PublicIdentifier.base:
Server-generated public identifier. This is a URN, NOT an ARN: the public identifier is a public-facing, provider-neutral name (a Record may be hosted outside AWS), so it deliberately does not use the arn: scheme.

Layout: urn:air:[<subdomain>.]<domain>:<namespace>:<identity>[;<kind>]

  • authority [<subdomain>.]<domain> — the publisher FQDN, with the optional subdomain folded in as a leading label (e.g. agents.acme.com; without a subdomain, just acme.com).
  • <namespace> — the association's category values concatenated with : (zero-or-more segments; absent when no categories were supplied).
  • <identity> — the Record name: letters, digits, ., _, / and -, as Vestry allows.
  • <kind> — the artifact kind from the Record's recordType (ai-catalog issue 59): MCP is mcp, AGENT and CUSTOM are agent, SKILL is skill, WEB_BOT is webbot. Absent for GATEWAY and when the association carried no recordType. The kind is part of the identifier, so urn:air:acme.com:x;mcp and urn:air:acme.com:x are two identifiers. Belfry mints ;; the pattern also admits #, +, $ and @, so identifiers minted with # before the delimiter settled on ; stay valid until they're re-minted. Examples: urn:air:acme.com:finance-agent (no subdomain/categories), urn:air:agents.acme.com:financial:money:finance-agent, urn:air:acme.com:weather;mcp.

refs.CreatePublisherResponse$status:
The domain verification status of the publisher:

  • ACTION_REQUIRED: The registry is waiting to find the DNS TXT record described by domainChallenge.
  • ACTIVE: The domain is verified. You can associate registry records with the publisher.
  • SUSPENDED: The domain was verified, but a later check found the TXT record missing or changed. The publisher returns to ACTIVE when the record is found again, and becomes FAILED if the record stays missing.
  • FAILED: Verification didn't succeed, for example because the TXT record wasn't found in time or another account verified the domain first. Call ValidatePublisher to try again.
  • DELETING: A delete is in progress.
